blocks.text: Lesson 4 — Network fundamentals, segmentation and firewalls

LEARNING OUTCOME
Understand ports, protocols, trust zones and how to apply safe, staged firewall rules.

Safety rule: work only with devices, accounts and training applications you own or have explicit written permission to assess. Use synthetic information. A public system or a suspicious person is not permission.

An IP address identifies a network interface in context; a port identifies an application endpoint; a protocol defines communication behavior. An open port is not automatically a vulnerability. Determine whether the service is expected, patched, authenticated, monitored and reachable only by the intended clients.

blocks.text: A firewall evaluates traffic attributes such as direction, source, destination, protocol and port. Start from the service inventory, deny by default, and allow only required flows. Keep public web services separate from internal databases, administration paths and backups.

blocks.caption: Visual 3/6 — Firewall rule. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.
Visual 4/6 — Allow-list. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.

blocks.text: Before changing a remote firewall, verify recovery access, document dependencies, test in a lab and prepare a rollback. Check both IPv4 and IPv6 policy, inspect logs, and record exceptions with owners and expiry dates. An overly broad rule can cause outages even when it is not directly exploitable.

Visual 6/6 — Rule review. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.

blocks.text: Practice checklist: (1) read the lab rules, (2) use fabricated data or an isolated training target, (3) predict what the control should do, (4) test one small condition, (5) save only minimal evidence, and (6) explain the defensive follow-up. Stop and ask the owner if any target or action is outside the approved scope.

blocks.question: What is a sound default firewall posture?
options: Deny by default and allow required traffic
blocks.explanation: Default-deny reduces exposure while documented rules allow required services.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What is the purpose of segmentation?
blocks.explanation: Segmentation helps contain lateral movement and separate trust levels.
